thread:
alex.j: Quick question — custody arrangement changed midyear and we split weekdays. Can I add my child to my Redwood benefits now? Also how do we decide primary vs secondary insurer and what proof do you need?

maria.peopleops: Hey Alex — yes, custody change can be a Qualifying Life Event (QLE). You have 30 days from the event to submit the request + docs. Primary/secondary is handled by COB rules (usually the 'birthday rule' for parents). Short version: the parent whose birth month/day comes earlier in the calendar year is typically the primary for the child.

alex.j: Got it — so if my birthday is Jan and my ex is Aug, mine is primary. Does that apply to medical, dental, and vision all the same?

maria.peopleops: Mostly yes — medical plans follow the same COB order. Some ancillary plans behave differently but in practice carriers use the same coordination order. If you want us to confirm for a specific carrier we can check.

alex.j: What proofs are acceptable for the custody change? court order? signed parenting plan? handwritten note?

maria.peopleops: Acceptable docs (most common):
- court order/parenting plan showing custody change
- signed notarized agreement between parents
- school records or DMV with child at your address (if residency is the reason)
- court filing receipt if final order is pending (we can provisionally enroll, carrier may follow up)

maria.peopleops: To submit: email benefits@redwood.com with subject line exactly: "QLE: Add dependent — custody change — <employee name>" and attach PDFs. Or upload via the People Ops portal > Benefits > QLE uploads. Our benefits-bot will ack the file.

benefits-bot: Thanks! We received your upload (if attached) and assigned case #RB-2143. Carrier verification may take 5-10 business days.

alex.j: How does payroll proration work? If added mid-month, will I be charged full month?

maria.peopleops: Carriers vary. Typical outcomes:
- If processed within the carrier's cutoff for that month, coverage can be effective as of the custody change date (prorated premium from that date).
- If not, effective date may be the 1st of next month (no retro premium). We will estimate payroll deduction and share a final proration amount before changes hit payroll.

alex.j: Any impact on claims already paid by ex's plan? We might need coordination for an upcoming appointment next week.

tom.broker: If your plan becomes primary, submit a claim to primary first. If ex's plan already paid, secondary can seek balance. For urgent appt, we can request a predetermination/coverage letter from the carrier — send me the provider name/date and I can open the paperwork.

alex.j: Thanks. I'll gather the court order and email benefits@redwood.com now. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

maria.peopleops: Great — ping me here after you send it if you want me to confirm receipt. We're happy to scope the effective date with the carrier. :wave:
